title: eLocust3m and AI data cleaning feed FAO's East Africa locust control, which may have averted USD 1.56 billion in losses
summary: PlantVillage's app, built with FAO in under a month in 2020, gathered 240,000+ records; AI removed unusable data; FAO credits the tech-enabled operation with averting USD 1.56 billion in losses.
account: When desert locust swarms swept the Horn of Africa in early 2020, FAO's senior locust forecaster Keith Cressman asked Penn State's PlantVillage, which had built FAO's fall armyworm app, to adapt it; eLocust3M was released on Google Play on 20 February 2020 so that anyone with a smartphone could record georeferenced locust sightings, with photos checked by algorithms. Penn State also extended a deep-learning soil-moisture model to the affected region. FAO reported receiving up to 2,500 records a day, nearly 25 percent unusable or incorrect, and turned to PlantVillage to use artificial intelligence to identify and remove the unwanted data before sharing locations with ground and air control teams; the New York Times reported more than 240,000 records collected in a year by PlantVillage scouts, government personnel and citizens. The wider operation also used Garmin satellite devices, EarthRanger (Vulcan) and 28 aircraft coordinated with 51 Degrees. FAO's 6 May 2021 feature says control operations in East Africa prevented the loss of 4 million tonnes of cereal and 800 million liters of milk, protected the food security of 36.6 million people and avoided USD 1.56 billion in losses; the Times quoted FAO's estimate of USD 1.5 billion averted since February 2020 and FAO's Cyril Ferrand saying swarms were prevented from spilling into the Sahel. The date is FAO's feature date.
purpose: Collect georeferenced locust sightings from anyone with a smartphone and automatically check photos and remove unusable records so that FAO can direct survey and control teams.
system: eLocust3m (PlantVillage) with AI data validation feeding FAO's Desert Locust Information Service
developer: PlantVillage, Pennsylvania State University, with FAO
deployer: FAO Desert Locust Information Service and national locust control operations in Kenya, Ethiopia and Somalia
taxonomy_note: Loose fit; the AI cleaned one data stream in a wider operation, and the averted-loss figure is FAO's estimate for the whole effort.

ratings.reason: FAO states that East African control operations prevented the loss of 4 million tonnes of cereal and 800 million liters of milk and protected 36.6 million people's food security; the Times quotes FAO's USD 1.5 billion averted since February 2020. These are estimates for the whole operation of which the AI data pipeline was one part.

FAO received up to 2,500 records a day with nearly 25 percent unusable; PlantVillage's AI removed the unwanted data, and over 240,000 records were collected in a year from scouts and citizens who could not have used the discontinued eLocust3 tablets.
No individually documented farmer outcome in the fetched sources.

ai_role.statement: Two AI uses are documented: algorithms that double-check submitted photos (Times) and AI that filters unusable records out of FAO's daily intake (FAO); a Penn State deep-learning soil-moisture model is mentioned by the maker's university. The outcome figures belong to the entire control operation and no source isolates the AI's contribution. FAO is both co-developer and deployer, so its feature is maker-authored; the Times report is independent with named sources (Cressman, Ferrand, Hughes, Jeptoo, Owuor, Craig).

produced_by: An upsurge with swarms across Kenya, Ethiopia and Somalia in 2020 and no trained locust trackers in those countries
An existing FAO-PlantVillage app blueprint (fall armyworm) adaptable in under a month
Scouts recruited and trained by PlantVillage and governments
Aerial control assets (28 aircraft) coordinated through EarthRanger with 51 Degrees
must_hold: Smartphone coverage among scouts, with Garmin satellite devices where there is no network
FAO's Desert Locust Information Service acting on records daily
Control teams and aircraft available to act on reported locations

East Africa: icipe MaxEnt prediction of breeding regions
echoes.source: Kimathi et al. 2020, Scientific Reports, doi:10.1038/s41598-020-68895-2

headline: Locust control fed by eLocust3m may have averted USD 1.56 billion
metric: protected the food security of 36.6 million people and avoided USD 1.56 billion in losses

comparator.against: no locust control operations in East Africa (FAO's estimate of the losses that the control campaign averted)
comparator.before: loss of 4 million tonnes of cereal and 800 million litres of milk production, USD 1.56 billion in cereal and milk losses
comparator.after: those losses prevented and the food security of 36.6 million people protected
comparator.quote: In East Africa locust control operations have prevented the loss of 4 million tonnes of cereal and 800 million litres of milk production, while protecting the food security of 36.6 million people and avoiding USD 1.56 billion in cereal and milk losses.

later.note: In June 2022 FAO declared the East Africa upsurge over and said it had trained 3,800 people across the region to use applications such as eLocust3 to report locusts.
later.quote: We have trained 3 800 people in the entire region on how to use innovative applications such as eLocust3 to recognize and report on Desert Locust.

value.what: cereal and milk losses avoided by the locust control operations in East Africa that the app and AI data cleaning fed
value.who: East African farmers and herders (the food security of 36.6 million people)
value.quote: In East Africa locust control operations have prevented the loss of 4 million tonnes of cereal and 800 million litres of milk production, while protecting the food security of 36.6 million people and avoiding USD 1.56 billion in cereal and milk losses.
